questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

__No sooner did he finished__ his examination than he left for his cricket training centre.

options.text: no sooner than he did finished

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: no sooner did he finish.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence contains an error with the use of the verb **"finished"** after **"did."**
 
• When **"did"** is used as an **auxiliary verb**, the **main verb** should be in its **base form **(finish).
 
• The correct construction after "no sooner did" is to use the base form of the verb, which is "finish" in this case.
 
• The phrase "no sooner did he finish" correctly follows the rule of using the base form of the verb after "did."

Therefore, the correct answer is no sooner did he finish.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2: "no sooner than he finished" - Incorrect because** "no sooner" **should be followed by** "did"** and then the** base form** of the **verb**.
 
• Option 3: "no sooner than he did finished" - Incorrect as it redundantly uses **"did" **and **"finished" **together.
 
• Option 4: "no sooner had he finish" - Incorrect because **"had"** should be followed by the **past participle** **"finished,"** not the base form "finish."

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 4' i.e. 'after the breakfast' has an error.

• The phrase **"after the breakfast"** is incorrect because "breakfast" is an **uncountable noun** and should not have the definite article **"the"** before it.
 
• The correct phrase should be "after breakfast" without the article "the".
 
• Using "the" implies a specific breakfast, which is not the case here.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *They will start their journey after breakfast*.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

They had been dancing / for an hour / when our dance teacher / had arrived.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **had arrived**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence uses the** past perfect continuous tense** ("had been dancing") to describe an action that was ongoing in the past.
 
• The phrase "when our dance teacher had arrived" incorrectly uses the past perfect tense ("had arrived") instead of the **simple past tense**.
 
• The correct phrase should be "when our dance teacher arrived" to indicate that the arrival of the dance teacher interrupted the ongoing action of dancing.
 
• The sentence contains two clauses: the main clause and the subordinate (dependent) clause.
 
 
• Main clause: "They had been dancing for an hour"
 
• Subordinate clause: "when our dance teacher arrived"
 
 
 
• The use of the **past simple tense** in the **subordinate clause** (arrived) is essential because it marks the specific point in time at which the ongoing action (dancing) met an interruption or new event.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Correct sentence: *They had been dancing for an hour when our dance teacher arrived.*
